faq.q: What is the minimum cost for a stag yacht charter in Marbella?
faq.a: The cheapest option is the Astondoa 40 or Azimut 39 at €749 for 2 hours, including skipper, fuel, drinks, snacks, and VAT. For a longer trip, the 8-hour charter is €2,299.

faq.q: Can we bring our own food and decorations?
faq.a: Yes, you can bring your own food and decorations (e.g., stag banners, balloons) on board. Just coordinate with the crew beforehand. The boat already includes light snacks and drinks.

faq.q: How many people can join a stag yacht charter?
faq.a: Our fleet accommodates 5 to 12 passengers. The Dubhe (8m) holds 5, while the Ferretti 94 (29m) and Canados 86 (26m) each hold 12. Check individual boat specs for exact capacity.

faq.q: Is a skipper included, and do we need a licence?
faq.a: Yes, every charter includes a licensed skipper who handles navigation and safety. You don't need a boating licence – just relax and enjoy.

faq.q: What is the best time of year for a stag weekend in Marbella?
faq.a: May to October offers warm weather (25–30°C) and calm seas. July and August are peak, so book early. April and November are cooler but still pleasant.

faq.q: Can we swim, snorkel, or use water toys?
faq.a: Absolutely. Most charters include stops for swimming at spots like Cala del Faro or Cala Cortés. Jet skis are available on the Mangusta 80, and other water toys can be arranged on request.

faq.q: How do we book and pay?
faq.a: Contact us via WhatsApp for availability and pricing. A deposit (typically 50%) secures the booking, with the balance due 7 days before departure. We accept bank transfer or card.

faq.q: What happens if the weather is bad?
faq.a: The skipper assesses conditions on the day. If it's unsafe, we reschedule or offer a full refund. We don't sail in storms or high winds.

data.body_html:
Planning a stag weekend in Marbella for 2031? A private yacht charter is the ultimate way to celebrate, combining luxury, sun, and the Costa del Sol coastline. This guide breaks down the costs, boat options, and what’s included so you can budget accurately. Whether you’re 5 or 12 lads, we’ve got a boat to fit your group and your wallet.

Why Choose a Yacht Charter for a Stag Weekend in Marbella?

Marbella’s coastline offers 27 km of beaches, hidden coves, and glamorous marinas. A private charter gives you exclusive space to party, swim, and enjoy the scenery without crowds. You control the itinerary: cruise past the Golden Mile, anchor at Cabopino, or visit Estepona. Plus, all our charters include a skipper, fuel, drinks, and snacks – no hidden costs.

Cost Breakdown by Boat Tier

Our fleet is divided into three pricing tiers. Here’s what you can expect to spend:

Astondoa 40 / Azimut 399–11 pax2h€749
Astondoa 40 / Azimut 399–11 pax8h€2,299
Mangusta 80 (any variant)12 pax4h minimum€4,719 (includes jet ski)
Other boats (e.g., Ferretti 94, Canados 86)10–12 paxCustomPricing on request via WhatsApp

For larger groups or longer trips, contact us for a custom quote. We also offer half-day (4h) and full-day (8h) options for most vessels.

What’s Included in Every Charter?

All our stag charters include: licensed skipper, fuel, insurance, safety equipment, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks, and Spanish VAT (21%). No surprise charges. You just show up at Puerto Banús and enjoy.

How to Budget for Extras

While the charter covers basics, you might want: premium catering (€20–40/person), extra water toys (jet ski, paddleboard – €150–300), or a photographer (€200–400). Tips for the crew are optional but appreciated (10–15% of charter fee).

Best Boats for a Stag Do

For a small group (5–8), the Marbella yacht charter options like the Bandido (8 pax) or Pershing 46 (10 pax) are sporty and fast. For 12 lads, the Mangusta 80 (24m) or Ferretti 94 (29m) offer decks for partying and a free jet ski. The Azimut 58 Flybridge has a spacious flybridge for sunbathing.

Sample Itinerary for a Stag Yacht Charter

Depart Puerto Banús at 11:00. Cruise east past Marbella Marina and the Golden Mile. Anchor at Cala del Faro for swimming and snorkelling (1 hour). Lunch on board (bring your own or order catering). Head to Cabopino for a beach stop. Return to Puerto Banús by 18:00 for sunset drinks. Total cost for 10 people on an Astondoa 40 (8h): €2,299, or €230 per person.

When to Book for 2031

Peak season (June–September) books up 4–8 weeks in advance. For a weekend in July 2031, start enquiries by April. Off-peak (May, October) offers better availability and slightly lower demand. Always confirm your date via WhatsApp.

Frequently asked questions

What is the minimum cost for a stag yacht charter in Marbella?

The cheapest option is the Astondoa 40 or Azimut 39 at €749 for 2 hours, including skipper, fuel, drinks, snacks, and VAT. For a longer trip, the 8-hour charter is €2,299.

Can we bring our own food and decorations?

Yes, you can bring your own food and decorations (e.g., stag banners, balloons) on board. Just coordinate with the crew beforehand. The boat already includes light snacks and drinks.

How many people can join a stag yacht charter?

Our fleet accommodates 5 to 12 passengers. The Dubhe (8m) holds 5, while the Ferretti 94 (29m) and Canados 86 (26m) each hold 12. Check individual boat specs for exact capacity.

Is a skipper included, and do we need a licence?

Yes, every charter includes a licensed skipper who handles navigation and safety. You don't need a boating licence – just relax and enjoy.

What is the best time of year for a stag weekend in Marbella?

May to October offers warm weather (25–30°C) and calm seas. July and August are peak, so book early. April and November are cooler but still pleasant.

Can we swim, snorkel, or use water toys?

Absolutely. Most charters include stops for swimming at spots like Cala del Faro or Cala Cortés. Jet skis are available on the Mangusta 80, and other water toys can be arranged on request.

How do we book and pay?

Contact us via WhatsApp for availability and pricing. A deposit (typically 50%) secures the booking, with the balance due 7 days before departure. We accept bank transfer or card.

What happens if the weather is bad?

The skipper assesses conditions on the day. If it's unsafe, we reschedule or offer a full refund. We don't sail in storms or high winds.
